title: Compile orchestration and pinning workflow for adaptive MHA/GQA/MoE kernels
creator: Aisha Park
description: Scope: Build an orchestration layer and safe pinning workflow that allows per-model adaptive kernel selection and pin publishing for MHA, GQA, and MoE architectures. This ticket covers: 1) compilation signature generation and provenance, 2) automated preflight validation across representative microbenchmarks (latency, throughput, memory), 3) publishing pinned performance profiles to the registry, and 4) canary + rollback safeguards integrated with the rollout controller. Goals: - Ensure new compile profiles optimize for target SLOs without regression in correctness metrics (logprob/likelihood delta threshold) - Provide a machine-readable manifest (signature + fingerprint) that the serving runtime uses for safe pin selection - Bake in automatic fallback to compatible profiles when pinned variants fail or increase latency/failure rates - Instrument telemetry and alerting tied to profile rollouts Acceptance criteria: - Compile unit emits deterministic manifest (hash, toolchain version, compile-time flags) and stores provenance in registry - Preflight suite executes on a 3-node representative harness and reports p50/p99 latency, tokens/sec, memory, and correctness checks; failures block publish - Publishing API accepts a manifest and marks it staged; staged profiles can be promoted to global after canary window with health checks - Rollout controller supports canary percentage, automatic metrics-based promotion, and automated rollback with clear audit trail Non-goals: - Building a new autotuner; this work uses existing autotune outputs and wraps them in the orchestration flow. Success metrics: - 95% of new model pins pass preflight on first try for standard MHA/GQA shapes - Reduction in manual rollbacks by 80% vs baseline in the quarter - Mean time to detect a bad pin during canary < 15 minutes
comments: 2025-02-11 — Kickoff: Reviewed current compile pipeline. Core gap: we don’t persist toolchain provenance with compiled kernels. Action: add signature layer to compiler output (Mateo)

2025-02-18 — Design review with Research and Infra: decided on manifest schema fields: model_arch, shape_signature, compile_hash, toolchain_version, quantization_profile, hardware_targets, perf_baseline_id. Hold minimal viability in runtime: only compare compile_hash + hardware_targets on startup.

2025-02-22 — Engineering spike: implemented prototype signature generator in compile agent (branch: feat/compile-signature). Microbenchmark harness added to CI (github.com/redwood-inference/bench/PR-412). Initial run shows MHA shapes p99 regression ~4% for nvlink-optimizations flagged; flagged for further kernel parameter tuning.
2025-02-26 — PM feedback (Jordan): require explicit canary window and alert mapping to oncall. Added canary_steps to manifest and integration with Rollouts service.
2025-03-01 — Security review in progress: compilation provenance will be stored in internal registry (encrypted at rest); design doc shared to Confluence for compliance review.

2025-03-03 — QA: preflight harness found a correctness delta for a sparse MoE routing case when using pack-vec kernels. Root cause: small quantization mismatch; mitigation: add an extra FP32 verification pass for MoE routes in preflight. Assigned to @li-wang.

2025-03-04 — Decision: block global publish if any correctness check fails or if runtime error rate > 0.5% during canary. Canary default window = 30 minutes or 10k requests. Mateo to add automatic rollback playbook.
decision_log: Use compile_hash + toolchain_version as primary immutable identifier; allow secondary tags for performance metadata.
Default canary to 10% traffic for 30 minutes with automated rollback triggers: increased p50 by >20% or error_rate >0.5% or model-accuracy-regression >0.2 logprob.
Preflight must include a short FP32 verification pass for MoE routing and a full-run sampling for GQA shapes to catch sparse attention regressions.
runbook: How to pause a rollout: POST /rollouts/{id}/pause — requires SRE or release-engineer.
Emergency rollback: POST /rollouts/{id}/rollback — will rebind to previous pinned profile and notify oncall. Run the rollback validation job and file incident with perf traces.
If canary error rate spikes: reduce canary to 0% immediately, open incident, and attach compile manifest to incident ticket for root cause.
Postmortem checklist: collect compile manifest, preflight logs, canary telemetry, and kernel build logs; tag with release and commit SHA.
